subtitle.bold: who can access your server from the internet
subtitle.post: . Apply a preset or add a custom rule.

info.mid: . Your active SSH or panel session will remain connected. Protected ports

close_mysql.name: Close External MySQL Access
close_mysql.description: Closes database port 3306 to the internet. MySQL remains accessible from the server.

close_ftp.name: Close FTP
close_ftp.description: Closes FTP port 21. You can safely close FTP if you use SFTP.

close_mail.name: Close Mail Ports
close_mail.description: Closes SMTP, POP3, and IMAP ports. This reduces spam relay risk when no mail server is present.

close_rpc.name: Close RPC / NFS
close_rpc.description: Closes rpcbind port 111 and NFS port 2049 when file sharing is not in use.

ban.name: Block IP
ban.description: Block a specific IP address. Enter a port to block access only to that port, or leave it blank to block access to all ports.
ban.example: Example: Completely block 45.9.1.2 after repeated SSH attempts.

whitelist.name: Allow IP
whitelist.description: Enter a port to allow access only from these IP addresses and block everyone else. Leave the port blank to give this IP priority access to all ports.
whitelist.example: Example: Enter port 8443 and your office IP so only you can access the panel.

close.name: Close Port
close.description: Close a port to everyone except allowlisted addresses. Critical ports for SSH, web, the panel, and DNS are protected and cannot be closed.
close.example: Example: Close database port 3306 to external access.

form.step1: 1. What do you want to do?
form.notePlaceholder: e.g. IP attempting SSH brute force

warning.mid: This port will be open only to the IP address above. If your IP is

preview.closeReady: Port {{port}} will be closed to everyone except allowlisted addresses.
preview.banPort: {{address}} will be blocked from accessing port {{port}}.
preview.banAll: {{address}} will be blocked from accessing all ports.
preview.whitelistPort: Port {{port}} will be open only to {{address}}. Everyone else will be blocked.
preview.whitelistAll: {{address}} will have priority access to all ports.

rules.title: Active Rules
rules.emptyTitle: No rules yet. The server is open to all connections.
rules.emptyHint: Apply a preset above to get started.

success.templateAlreadyApplied: "{{name}}" is already applied. No new rules were added.
success.ruleAdded: The rule was added and applied to the firewall.

geo.sectionHint: Drops every packet from a country at the firewall. This covers every port, including SSH, mail and FTP, not only the web server.

credentials.title: MaxMind account
credentials.hint: Country data comes from MaxMind GeoLite2. Create a free account, accept its licence, then paste the account ID and a licence key here. Without them this feature stays off.
credentials.keyStored: A key is stored and is never shown again

confirm.block: Block every address in {{country}}? This closes every port on the server to that country, including SSH.

success.credentialsCleared: The MaxMind account was removed. Country blocking is now off.
success.updated: The country database was downloaded. Edition: {{date}}.
success.blocked: {{country}} is now blocked on every port.

error.credentials: Could not save the MaxMind account
error.update: Could not download the country database
error.unblock: Could not remove the country block

reasons.geoip_unavailable: No country database has been downloaded yet. Save a MaxMind account and download it first.
reasons.country_unknown: The country database does not carry that country.

geo.noteAllPorts: The block applies to every port, so a blocked country loses SSH, mail and FTP as well as the website.
geo.noteWhitelist: The country block is evaluated before the allowlist, so allowing a single address cannot reopen a blocked country.
geo.noteApproximate: GeoLite2 is approximate and carries wrong records even at country level. Use IP rules where the decision must be exact.
